title: Dal Makhani
subtitle: Punjabi slow-cooked black lentil and kidney bean dal
excerpt: The great Punjabi dal: whole black lentils and kidney beans slow-cooked overnight with tomato, butter, and cream into a silky, extraordinarily rich dal that is the speciality of Delhi's most famous restaurants.

recipe.sourceNotes: Dal makhani (literally 'buttery lentils') is one of the most celebrated dishes of Punjabi cuisine and North Indian cooking, associated particularly with the restaurants of Delhi, where Moti Mahal restaurant famously popularised the dish in the 1950s. The dal is made from whole black urad lentils (black gram) and kidney beans, cooked at length in a tomato-based sauce with an extraordinary amount of butter and cream. The cooking time is one of its defining features: the authentic version is cooked on a low flame for 8 to 12 hours in a tandoor's residual heat until the lentils break down into a thick, silky consistency. A home version achieves a comparable result with a long, slow oven braise or pressure cooker. The dish should be rich, buttery, and deeply savoury.

content.text: Soak the lentils overnight; they take significantly longer to cook than green or red lentils. The long cooking time is what creates the silky, almost creamy consistency; do not rush it. Add the butter and cream at the end only, not during cooking. Season with salt only after the lentils are fully tender; salt added early slows the cooking.

items.preparation: whole black urad; soaked overnight; drained

content.text: Drain the soaked lentils and place in a large pot. Cover with plenty of cold water and bring to a boil. Simmer for 45 to 60 minutes until nearly tender. Drain and set aside.
Fry the onion in the oil for 10 minutes until golden. Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, garam masala, and chilli powder. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes. Simmer for 10 minutes.

Add the lentils, kidney beans, and 300 ml water. Stir, season with salt. Simmer on the lowest heat for 45 to 60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until very thick and silky. Stir in the butter and cream. Simmer for 5 more minutes. Garnish with coriander and serve with naan or rice.
